sub: Measure once, check four things, and know when to take it off

cards.title: Measure, Don't Guess
rows: Two fingers flat under every strap

cards.title: Wear Time
rows: Shorter again, and never warm days
Must come off in one pull

cards.title: Must Stay Clear
list: Eyes — a dog that cannot see cannot read other dogs
Ears — covering them removes early warning
Nose and mouth — panting is how dogs cool down
Full movement: walk, sit, lie, turn, squat
Nothing small enough to swallow: bells, buttons, eyes
No drawstrings, elastic or rubber bands

cards.title: By Species
rows: Yes, if it fits and they accept it
Never — air sacs need the chest free
Never — it blocks their heat source

cards.title: Comfortable
list: Moves at a normal pace, normal stride
Sits and lies down without hesitating
Loose body, tail carried as usual
Comes to you, or starts play
Ignores the costume rather than attending to it

cards.title: Take It Off Now
list: FREEZING — the most misread signal there is
Panting with no heat or exercise
Whale eye — whites showing at the side
Ears flat back, tail tucked, body low
Lip licking, repeated yawning, head turning away
Chewing a strap, or backing out of it

rules: Measure the chest, not the dog.
A 25 lb beagle and a 25 lb whippet are the same on the scale and inches apart around the ribs.
Never leave them alone in it.
A strap catches on a crate door, the pet panics, and a tangled animal can strangle or chew and swallow part of it.
Freezing is distress, not good behavior.
Stillness is what an animal does when it cannot work out how to escape. Costume off.
Two weeks of rehearsal, 30 seconds at a time.
A costume worn first on the night stacks three stressors at once.
If they fail the towel test, buy a bandana.
It photographs better than a costume they are enduring, and there is no prize for the full outfit.
